Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 54, verse 1:

(p-476) In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

Surah al-Qamar (The Moon).

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿The Hour has drawn near﴾.

We have already presented the verses that clarify this in the beginning of Surah an-Nahl, in the discussion of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿The command of Allah has come﴾, and elsewhere in other places.

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And if they see a sign, they turn away﴾. We have already presented the verses that clarify this in Surah al-An'am, in the discussion of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And had We sent down to you a written scroll on paper, and they touched it with their hands﴾.

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿They will come forth from the graves as if they were scattered locusts, hastening toward the caller﴾.

We have already presented the verses that clarify this in Surah Ya-Sin, in the discussion of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And when they come out of the graves to their Lord, they will hasten forth﴾ [Ya-Sin: 51], and in Surah Qaf, in the discussion of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿On the Day the earth will split asunder from them, rushing forth﴾ [Qaf: 44].

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 54, verse 8:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿The disbelievers will say, "This is a difficult day."﴾

We have already presented the verses that clarify this in Surat al-Furqan, in the discussion of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿The companions of the Garden on that Day will have a better resting place and a finer place of repose﴾ [al-Furqan: 24], and in Surat al-Hajj, in the discussion of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And indeed, a day with your Lord is like a thousand years of what you count﴾ [al-Hajj: 47].

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And indeed, a day with your Lord is like a thousand years of what you count﴾.

Ibn ʿAmir read this letter (فَفَتَحْنا, fafatahna, "and We opened") with the tā' doubled (fa-fattaḥnā), for intensification (lil-takthīr). The rest of the seven readers read it with the tā' single.

In this noble verse, may He be exalted, He mentions that His Prophet Noah called upon Him, saying that his people had overpowered him, asking his Lord to grant him victory over them. Allah granted him victory over them and destroyed them by drowning, because He, exalted is He, opened the gates of the heaven with pouring water, that is, water flowing forth and poured down abundantly, and He, exalted is He, caused the earth to gush forth springs.

His saying, ʿuyūnan (springs), is a tamyīz (specification accusative, a noun clarifying an element of the sentence) transformed from the object; the original was "We caused the springs of the earth to gush forth." Tafjīr (gushing forth) is bringing out water from it in abundance. The "al-" in His saying ﴿the waters met﴾ is for the genus (lil-jins, generic), and its meaning is that the water of the sky and the water of the earth met ﴿for a matter already decreed﴾, that is, Allah decreed and ordained it.

It has been said that its meaning is that the water descending from the sky and the water gushing from the earth were set by Allah in a measure such that neither of them exceeded the other. The first view is more apparent.

What this noble verse contains of Noah's supplication to his Lord, may He be exalted, that He grant him victory over his people and take vengeance upon them, and that Allah answered him and granted him victory over them, destroying them all by drowning in this water that met from the sky and the earth, has been clarified in other verses of the Book of Allah, such as His saying, exalted is He, concerning the Prophets: ﴿And Noah, when he called before; so We responded to him and saved him and his family from the great distress. And We helped him against the people who denied Our signs. Indeed, they were a people of evil, so We drowned them all﴾ [al-Anbiya': 76–77].

And His saying, exalted is He, in al-Saffat: ﴿And Noah had certainly called Us, and We are the best to respond. And We saved him and his family from the great distress. And We made his descendants the survivors. And We left for him among later generations: "Peace upon Noah among the worlds." Indeed, We thus reward the doers of good. Indeed, he was among Our believing servants. Then We drowned the others﴾ [al-Saffat: 75–82], up to His saying: ﴿Then We drowned the others﴾.

He, exalted is He, has made clear that Noah's supplication included his asking Allah to destroy them with total annihilation. Those verses contain an explanation of His saying here: ﴿So grant victory﴾, as in His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And Noah said, "My Lord, do not leave upon the earth from among the disbelievers any dweller. Indeed, if You leave them, they will mislead Your servants and will not beget except a wicked disbeliever"﴾ [Nuh: 26–27]. Noah did not invoke against his people except after Allah revealed to him that none of them would believe except those few who had already believed. This is in His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And it was revealed to Noah that none of your people will believe except those who have already believed﴾ [Hud: 36], and He, exalted is He, has said: ﴿And none believed with him except a few﴾ [Hud: 40].

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿ʿuyūnan﴾ (springs) was read by Ibn Kathir, by Ibn ʿAmir in the transmission of Ibn Dhakwan, by ʿĀṣim in the transmission of Shuʿba, by Ḥamza, and by al-Kisā'ī as ʿiyūnan (عِيُونًا) with a kasra on the ʿayn, for assimilation to the yā' (limujānasat al-yāʾ, for assimilation to the letter yā').

It was read by Nāfiʿ, Abū ʿAmr, Ibn ʿAmir in the transmission of Hishām, and ʿĀṣim in the transmission of Ḥafs as ʿuyūnan (عُيُونًا) with a ḍamma on the ʿayn, according to the original form.

(p-478) His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And We carried him upon [a vessel] of planks and nails﴾.

He does not specify here what the "planks" and "nails" are, but He clarifies in other places that what is meant is: "And We carried him upon a ship ﴿of planks﴾," that is, of wood, "﴿and nails﴾," that is, nails that bind some of the wood to other wood. The singular of ﴿dusur﴾ is disar, like kitab and kutub (book and books). This is the view of most of the exegetes.

Some scholars and some lexicographers said: the dusur are the cords with which the planks of the ship are tied together.

Some scholars said: the dusur are the prow of the ship, that is, its chest and front, with which it cleaves (tadsuru) the water, meaning it pushes and cuts through it. They said: it derives from al-dasr, which means pushing.

Among the verses indicating that "the vessel of planks and nails" is the ship is His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Indeed, when the water overflowed, We carried you in the flowing [vessel]﴾ [al-Haqqah: 11], that is, the ship, as we explained in Surat al-Shura in our discussion of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And among His signs are the ships in the sea like mountains﴾ [al-Shura: 32].

And His saying, exalted is He: ﴿So We saved him and the companions of the ship﴾ [al-Ankabut: 15], and His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And a sign for them is that We carried their offspring in the laden ship﴾ [Ya-Sin: 41], and other verses besides these.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 54, verse 15:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And We have left it as a sign, so is there any who will remember?﴾.

The pronoun in His saying, exalted is He, ﴿We have left it﴾, some of the scholars ('ulama') said: it refers to this great act which He performed upon the people of Nuh (Noah).

The meaning: And We have certainly left Our act upon the people of Nuh, and Our destruction of them, as a sign for those after them, so that they would be deterred and would refrain from denying the messengers, lest We do to them the like of what We did to the people of Nuh. That this act is a sign is stated by Him, exalted is He, in His saying: ﴿And the people of Nuh, when they denied the messengers, We drowned them and made them a sign for mankind﴾ [al-Furqan: 37], and His saying, exalted is He: ﴿So We saved him and those with him in the laden ship. Then We drowned the rest afterward. Indeed in that is a sign, but most of them were not believers﴾ [al-Shu'ara': 119-121].

Some of the scholars said: the pronoun in ﴿We have left it﴾ refers to the ship, and that the ship of Nuh being a sign is made clear by Allah, exalted is He, in verses of His Book, such as His saying, exalted is He: ﴿So We saved him and the companions of the ship, and made it a sign for the worlds﴾ [al-'Ankabut: 15], and His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And a sign for them is that We carried their offspring in the laden ship, and We created for them of its likeness that which they ride﴾ [Ya-Sin: 41-42].

He, the Exalted, said: ﴿And We have certainly made the Qur'an easy for remembrance, so is there anyone who will remember?﴾

We have already given its explanation in Surah al-Qital (Surah 47), in our lengthy discussion on His statement, the Exalted: ﴿Then do they not reflect upon the Qur'an, or are there locks upon [their] hearts?﴾ [Muhammad: 24].

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 54, verse 19:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Indeed, We sent upon them a furious wind on a day of continuous misfortune.﴾

We have already presented the clear proofs concerning this, and the statements of the scholars (ahl al-'ilm) regarding the day of continuous misfortune (yawm al-nahs al-mustamirr), in Surah Fussilat, in the discussion of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿So We sent upon them a furious wind in days of misfortune﴾ [Fussilat: 16].

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 54, verse 24:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿So they said, "Shall we follow a single human being from among us?"﴾. And His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Has the Reminder been sent down to him from among us?﴾.

We have already presented the verses that clarify these two statements in the discussion of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And they wonder that a warner has come to them from among themselves﴾ [Sad: 4], and His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Has the Reminder been sent down to him from among us? Rather, they are in doubt about My Reminder﴾ [Sad: 8], and the verse that follows it.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 54, verse 28:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And inform them that the water is to be shared between them, each share being attended⦗by its turn⦘﴾.

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And inform them that the water is to be shared between them, each share being attended﴾ means: inform them, O Salih, the people of Thamud, that the water, which is the water of the well from which the she-camel used to drink, is to be shared between them, so that one day is for the she-camel and one day is for Thamud. So His saying "between them" means between the she-camel and Thamud, and He gave the rational beings precedence over the she-camel. ﴿Each share being attended﴾ means that its owner attends it, so the she-camel attends its day's drink and Thamud attends its day's drink.

What this noble verse includes is clarified in another verse, His saying in ash-Shu'ara': ﴿He said: This is a she-camel; she has a drink, and you have a drink on a known day﴾ [ash-Shu'ara' 26:155]. The drink of the she-camel is what Salih warned them against, so that they would not interfere with it, in His saying: ﴿Then the Messenger of Allah said to them: the she-camel of Allah, and her drink﴾ [ash-Shams 91:13].

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 54, verse 29:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿So they called their companion, and he took [the sword] and hamstrung [the she-camel]﴾.

His saying: ﴿fa-ta'ātā﴾ (and he took [it] up). Abu Hayyan said in al-Bahr: "fa-ta'ātā is the reflexive form (muṭāwi') of ʿāṭā, and it is as if this act was passed among the people, and some of them handed it to others, so Qudar took it up and grasped the hamstringing with his hand." End of the point of relevance from it.

The Arabs say: ta'ātā kadhā (he undertook such a thing) when he did it or took it up, and ʿāṭāhu (he handed it to him) when he took it. From this is the saying of Hassan, may Allah be pleased with him:

"Both of them milked the juice, and he handed me a cup, the one more loosened for the joint."

As for his saying: fa-ʿaqara (and he hamstrung), meaning: he undertook the hamstringing of the she-camel and hamstrung her. The two verbs' objects are thus omitted, their estimate being as we have mentioned. He referred to the hamstringer of the she-camel here as "their companion," and he referred to him in al-Shams as "the most wretched of them," in His saying: ﴿When the most wretched of them set off﴾ [al-Shams: 14].

This noble verse points to the removal of a well-known difficulty in the verse. Its explanation is that Allah, may He be exalted, attributed the hamstringing in it to one person, not to a group, for He said: ﴿So he took [it] up and hamstrung﴾ in the singular, although He attributed the hamstringing of the she-camel in other verses to all of Thamud:

• as in His saying in Surat al-A'raf: ﴿So they hamstrung the she-camel and defied the command of their Lord﴾ [al-A'raf: 77] and so on,

• and His saying, may He be exalted, in Hud: ﴿So they hamstrung her, and he said: "Enjoy yourselves in your homes for three days"﴾ [Hud: 65],

• and His saying in al-Shu'ara': ﴿So they hamstrung her, and then they became regretful﴾ [al-Shu'ara': 157],

• and His saying in al-Shams: ﴿So they denied him and hamstrung her﴾ [al-Shams: 14].

The way in which this verse points to the removal of this difficulty is that His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿So they called their companion, and he took [it] up and hamstrung﴾ indicates that all of Thamud agreed together on hamstringing the she-camel, so they called one of them to carry out what they had agreed upon, acting originally for himself and vicariously for others. It is known that those who colluded in the hamstringing are all hamstringers, and the attribution of the hamstringing is correct both to the one who directly carried it out and to all of them, because they colluded, as is shown by the sequence of the taking up of the hamstringing with fa- (then) in His saying ﴿fa-ta'ātā fa-ʿaqara﴾ after their calling their companion, so that he would stand in for them in the direct performance of the hamstringing, in His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿So they called their companion﴾, meaning: they called him so that he would hamstring her.

Some scholars reconciled these verses in another way, namely that the use of the plural to mean some of them is a well-known Arabic idiom, and it is frequent in the Qur'an and in Arabic speech.

We have already mentioned in Surat al-Hujurat that among its instances is the reading of Hamza in His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And if they fight you, then kill them﴾ [al-Baqarah: 191], in the form of the simple verb in both verbs, because one who has been killed and died cannot be commanded to kill his killer. Rather, the meaning is: if they kill some of you, then let some of you other kill them. A parallel to this is the saying of Ibn Mutiʿ:

"If you kill us at the lava field of Waqim, we are the first of those on Islam who were killed,"

meaning: if you kill some of us. Among its instances also is: ﴿The Bedouins say, "We have believed." Say, "You have not believed"﴾ [al-Hujurat: 14], because this applies to some of them and not others, as evidenced by His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And among the Bedouins is he who believes in Allah and the Last Day…﴾ up to His saying: ﴿Allah will admit them into His mercy; indeed Allah is Forgiving and Merciful﴾ [al-Tawbah: 99].

We have already mentioned in al-Hujurat and elsewhere that among the clearest Arabic evidences for this is the poet's saying:

"So the sword of Banu ʿAbs, when they struck with it, cut down from my hands the hand of Warqa' from the head of Khalid."

His saying, may He be exalted: fa-ʿaqara, meaning: he killed her. The Arabs use ʿaqr for killing, slaughtering and wounding. From this is the saying of Imru' al-Qays:

"She says, when the saddle leaned with us together, 'You have hamstrung my camel, O Imru' al-Qays, so dismount!'"

From the use of ʿaqr for slaughtering camels for the entertainment of a guest is the saying of Jarir:

"You count the hamstringing of the wolf the best of your glory, sons of Dhuwtara, were it not for the armoured warrior."

⁕ ⁕ ⁕

The author said in (Daf' Iham al-Idtirab 'an Ayat al-Kitab):

In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

Surat al-Qamar.

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿So they called their companion, and he took [it] up and hamstrung﴾.

It indicates that the hamstringer of the she-camel is one person, and other verses have come indicating that he was more than one, such as His saying: ﴿So they hamstrung the she-camel﴾ and so on [al-A'raf: 77], and His saying: ﴿So they denied him and hamstrung her﴾ [al-Shams: 14].

The answer is from two aspects:

The first: that they all colluded in hamstringing her, so the most wretched of them set off to carry out the act, and so the hamstringing was attributed to them because it was with their consent and collusion.

The second aspect: is what we mentioned in Surat "al-Anfal" regarding the attribution of the act to a group, meaning some of them. We mentioned in "al-Anfal" its parallels in the Great Qur'an, and knowledge is with Allah, may He be exalted.

The statement of Allah the Exalted: ﴿Indeed, We sent upon them one blast⁠﴾ [al-Qamar: 31].

We have already presented, at length, the verses that clarify this in Surat Fussilat, in the discussion of His saying, the Exalted: ﴿So the thunderbolt of the humiliating punishment seized them for what they used to earn⁠﴾ [Fussilat: 17].

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 54, verse 34:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Indeed, We sent upon them a storm of stones, except the family of Lot; We saved them at dawn﴾.

As for His saying ﴿Indeed, We sent upon them a storm of stones﴾: We have already presented the verses that clarify it in Surat al-Furqan, in the discussion of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And they have certainly passed by the town which was rained upon with an evil rain﴾ [al-Furqan: 40], and His saying ﴿except the family of Lot; We saved them at dawn﴾. We have already presented the verses that clarify it, with a thorough and abundant clarification.

(p-483) It has also included the clarification of the story of Lot and his people in Surat Hud and Surat al-Hijr, in the discussion of the story mentioned in the two surahs.

The commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 54, verse 41:

His statement, exalted is He: ﴿And the warnings had certainly come to the people of Pharaoh﴾ ﴿They denied Our signs, all of them, so We seized them with the seizure of One Almighty, Able.﴾ These two verses contain three matters:

The first: that the people of Pharaoh were visited by the warnings.

The second: that they denied the signs of Allah.

The third: that Allah seized them with the seizure of One Almighty, Able.

These three matters mentioned here are clarified in other verses of the Book of Allah.

As for the first of them, namely that the people of Pharaoh and his folk were visited by the warnings, Allah, exalted is He, clarified it in many verses of His Book.

Know first that His statement ﴿the warnings had come﴾ (al-nudhur) has been said to be the plural of nadhir (warner), meaning a messenger, and it has been said to be a verbal noun meaning warning (al-indhar). On the reading that it is a verbal noun, the Qur'anic verses clearly show in many places that the one who brought them that warning was Musa and Harun. On the reading that it is the plural of nadhir, meaning mundhir (one who warns), the intended referents are Musa and Harun. Many verses mention the sending of Musa and Harun to Pharaoh, such as His statement, exalted is He, in Ta-Ha: ﴿So go to him and say, "Indeed, we are two messengers of your Lord, so send with us the Children of Israel and do not torment them. We have certainly come to you with a sign from your Lord."﴾ [Ta-Ha: 47].

Then Allah clarified their warning to him in His statement: ﴿Indeed, it has been revealed to us that the punishment is for whoever denies and turns away﴾ [Ta-Ha: 48], and similar verses. In this verse there is a well-known question: Allah, blessed and exalted, sent two prophets to Pharaoh, Musa and Harun, as He said: ﴿So go to Pharaoh and say, "Indeed, we are messengers of the Lord of the worlds"﴾ [al-Shu'ara': 16]. Here He used the plural (nudhur) in His statement ﴿And the warnings had certainly come to the people of Pharaoh﴾. The scholars have several answers to this. One of them is that the least plural is two, as is established in the principles of Malik ibn Anas, may Allah have mercy on him. The author of Maraqi al-Su'ud expressed this in his verse:

"The least meaning of the plural, as is well known, is two, in the opinion of the Imam al-Himyari."

They said: and from this is His statement: ﴿Your hearts have certainly inclined﴾ [al-Tahrim: 4], where they have only two hearts. And His statement: ﴿But if he has brothers, then for his mother is a sixth﴾ [al-Nisa': 11], where "brothers" means two or more, as the Companions and those after them held, differing from Ibn Abbas. And His statement: ﴿and the ends of the day﴾ [Ta-Ha: 130], where it has two ends.

Another answer is what al-Zamakhshari and others mentioned: that the intended "warnings" are Musa, Harun, and other prophets, because they presented to them what the messengers had warned of. Another is that nudhur is a verbal noun meaning warning.

The author of this commentary, may Allah pardon him and forgive him, said: The correct answer is that whoever denies one messenger has denied all the messengers, and whoever denies one warner has denied all the warnings, because the core message of all the messengers is one, and it is the content of "There is no god but Allah," as He clarified in His statement: ﴿And We certainly sent into every nation a messenger, [saying], "Worship Allah and avoid the taghut"﴾ [al-Nahl: 36],

• and His statement: ﴿And We did not send before you any messenger except that We revealed to him that there is no god but I, so worship Me﴾ [al-Anbiya': 25],

• and His statement: ﴿And We did not send before you any messenger except that We revealed to him that there is no god but I, so worship Me﴾ [al-Zukhruf: 45].

Allah also clarified that whoever denies some of them has denied all of them, in His statement: ﴿And they say, "We believe in some and disbelieve in others," and they intend to adopt a way between that. Those are the true disbelievers﴾ [al-Nisa': 150], and He alluded to this in His statement: ﴿We make no distinction between any of His messengers﴾ [al-Baqarah: 285],

• and His statement: ﴿We make no distinction between any of them, and we are Muslims to Him﴾ [al-Baqarah: 136],

• and His statement, exalted is He: ﴿And those who believe in Allah and His messengers and do not distinguish between any of them — those, He will give them their rewards﴾ [al-Nisa': 152], to the end of the verse.

In Surah al-Shu'ara', Allah clarified that denying one messenger is denying all the messengers, in His statement: ﴿The people of Noah denied the messengers﴾ [al-Shu'ara': 105]. Then He made clear that their denial of the messengers occurred only through their denial of Noah alone, where He singled this out in His statement: ﴿When their brother Noah said to them, "Will you not fear Allah?"﴾ up to His statement: ﴿He said, "My Lord, indeed my people have denied me"﴾ [al-Shu'ara': 106–107]. Similarly, His statement: ﴿'Ad denied the messengers﴾ [al-Shu'ara': 123], then He made clear that this was through the denial of Hud alone, where He singled him out in His statement: ﴿When their brother Hud said to them, "Will you not fear Allah?"﴾ [al-Shu'ara': 124]. Likewise in His statement about the story of Salih and his people, and Lut and his people, and Shu'ayb and the People of the Thicket, as is known, and this is clear and has no obscurity. What makes this even clearer is his statement, peace and blessings be upon him: "We, the company of prophets, are half-brothers (awlad 'allat); our religion is one," meaning that they all agree on the fundamentals, even if their legislations differ in some of the subsidiary matters.

As for the second matter, namely that Pharaoh and his people denied the signs of Allah, this is clarified in other verses,

• such as His statement: ﴿And they said, "Whatever sign you bring us to bewitch us with, we will not believe in you."﴾ [al-A'raf: 132],

• and His statement: ﴿And We had certainly shown him all Our signs, but he denied and refused﴾ [Ta-Ha: 56],

• and His statement: ﴿Then he showed him the greatest sign. But he denied and disobeyed﴾ [al-Nazi'at: 20–21],

• and His statement: ﴿And put your hand into your garment; it will come out white without disease, among nine signs to Pharaoh and his people. Indeed, they were a defiantly disobedient people. But when Our signs came to them as perceivable evidence, they said, "This is obvious magic." And they rejected them, though their souls were convinced of them, out of wrongdoing and arrogance. So see how was the end of the corrupters﴾ [al-Naml: 12–14].

As for the third matter, namely His statement: ﴿So We seized them with the seizure of One Almighty, Able﴾, it is clarified in other verses of the Book of Allah,

• such as His statement: ﴿And [We left a sign] in Musa, when We sent him to Pharaoh with clear authority … so We seized him and his soldiers and threw them into the sea, while he was blameworthy﴾ [al-Dhariyat: 38–40],

• and His statement: ﴿Then Pharaoh followed them with his soldiers, and the sea covered them, that which covered them﴾ [Ta-Ha: 78],

• and His statement: ﴿And We drowned the people of Pharaoh while you were watching﴾ [al-Baqarah: 50],

and other verses besides these.

His statement ﴿the seizure of One Almighty, Able﴾ is clarified by His statement: ﴿And thus is the seizure of your Lord when He seizes the cities while they are wrongdoing. Indeed, His seizure is painful and severe﴾ [Hud: 102].

Al-Shaykhan (al-Bukhari and Muslim) narrated in their two Sahihs, from Abu Musa al-Ash'ari, may Allah be pleased with him, that the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said: "Indeed Allah gives respite to the wrongdoer, until when He seizes him, He does not let him go." Then he recited His statement: ﴿And thus is the seizure of your Lord when He seizes the cities﴾ to the end of the verse [Hud: 102]. Al-'Aziz means the Overpowering, and al-Muqtadir means One of great and immense power.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 54, verse 43:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Are your disbelievers better than those?﴾.

We have already presented the verses that clarify it in Surah az-Zukhruf, in the discussion of His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And We destroyed those who were stronger than them in might﴾ [az-Zukhruf: 8], and at the beginning of Surah ar-Rum, and in other places.

(p-486) His saying, exalted is He: ﴿On the Day they will be dragged into the Fire upon their faces: "Taste the touch of Saqar!"﴾

We have already presented the discussion of this in Surah At-Tur, in the discussion of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿On the Day they will be thrust into the fire of Hell with a violent thrust﴾ [At-Tur: 13].

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 54, verse 49:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Indeed, all things We have created in proportion.﴾

We have already discussed this in Surah al-Zukhruf, in some of the debates that we mentioned in the discussion of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Say: If the Most Merciful had a son, then I would be the first of the worshippers.﴾ [al-Zukhruf: 81]

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 54, verse 52:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And everything they have done is in the scriptures﴾ ﴿And every small and great thing is inscribed﴾.

The correct meaning of the verse is that everything the people have done is written against them ﴿in the scriptures﴾, which are the books of deeds (ṣuḥuf al-a'māl), ﴿and every small and great thing is inscribed﴾, meaning it is written against them, and nothing of it is left out.

This meaning is made clear in verses of the Book of Allah, such as His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And they will say, "Woe to us! What sort of record is this that leaves nothing small or great but has enumerated it?" And they will find what they did present [recorded]﴾ [al-Kahf: 49], and His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿The Day every soul will find what it has done of good present and what it has done of evil; it will wish that between it and that were a great distance﴾ [Ali 'Imran: 30].

Al-Zubur (zubur) is the plural of zabur, which means a book. Al-mustaṭar means al-mastur, that is, the written. Verses similar to this are many and well known.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 54, verse 54:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Indeed, the righteous will be in gardens and a river.﴾

That is, in gardens and rivers, as He, may He be exalted, made clear in His saying: ﴿Beneath which rivers flow﴾ [al-Baqarah: 25], and His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Therein are rivers of water unaltered, and rivers of milk whose taste does not change, and rivers of wine, delicious to the drinkers, and rivers of purified honey﴾ [Muhammad: 15].

We have already mentioned many examples of the use of the singular with the meaning of the plural, as here in the Noble Qur'an, whether the singular is indefinite, definite, or in construct (idafah). We also cited many Arabic examples of this in Surah al-Hajj, in the discussion of His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Then We bring you forth as a child﴾ [al-Hajj: 5], and elsewhere. And Allah, may He be exalted, knows best.

⁕ ⁕ ⁕

The author said in (Daf' Iham al-Idtirab 'an Ayat al-Kitab):

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Indeed, the righteous will be in gardens and a river.﴾

The manner of reconciling this with His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Therein are rivers of water unaltered﴾ [Muhammad: 15], and what follows, has already been explained.
